previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient, 21 days post orthotopic liver transplant for cryptogenic cirrhosis, was readmitted with fever, hypotension, and worsening back and abdominal pain. Imaging revealed left upper lobe ground-glass opacities consistent with early pneumonia and a large subphrenic fluid collection. He was started on Vancomycin and Cefepime based on prior Enterococcus bacteremia. A cervical spine MRI ruled out spinal infection, showing only degenerative changes. A PICC line was placed to complete intravenous antibiotic therapy at an extended care facility. His condition improved with treatment, inflammatory markers decreased, and he regained mobility with minimal assistance. He was discharged back to rehabilitation with plans for continued IV antibiotics, tube feeds, and close monitoring of transplant and metabolic parameters.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ man with elevated LFTs, mark the spot for liver
biopsy.

FINDINGS:  With the patient in end expiration and the right arm over the head,
a mark was made over the right lobe of the liver at the mid axillary line for
a biopsy to be performed by the clinical staff.

IMPRESSION:  Right lobe of the liver marked for biopsy to be performed by the
clinical staff.

AP CHEST, 2:41 P.M. ___  

HISTORY:  Assess PIC line.

IMPRESSION:  AP chest compared to ___:

Right PIC line extends as far as the low SVC.  Feeding tube is coiled in the
stomach and passes out of view.  Heart size top normal unchanged.  Band of
atelectasis at the base of the right lung are unchanged is the only focal
pulmonary abnormality.  No appreciable pleural effusion or evidence of central
adenopathy.  No pneumothorax.

HISTORY:  Patient with cirrhosis, elevated LFTs and altered mental status;
rule acute intracranial pathology.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar and multisequence MRI of the brain was performed
without intravenous contrast. According to the technologist's note scanned
into PACS, contrast could not be administered as the patient was not able to
remain still during the examination or complete the examination due to "severe
pain."

FINDINGS: There is no relevant prior imaging for comparison.

There is no acute intracranial infarct or hemorrhage. There is extensive,
confluent FLAIR- and T2-hyperintensity in subcortical and white matter,
representing the sequelae of chronic small vessel ischemic disease.  Similar
changes are also seen in the brainstem.  There is generalized volume loss of
the brain parenchyma.  There is no evidence of mass, mass effect, edema or
shift of normal midline structures.  

The paranasal sinuses are clear.  There is no abnormality of regional bone
marrow signal.

IMPRESSION: Limited (non-enhanced) study with no evidence of an acute
intracranial process, global atrophy and sequelae of chronic small vessel
ischemic disease.

HISTORY:  Patient with cirrhosis, elevated LFTs and tremor; rule out cervical
abnormality.

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal T1- and T2-weighted images of the cervical spine, only,
were obtained without intravenous contrast; axial sequences could not be
obtained. According to the technologist's note scanned into PACS, contrast
could not be administered, as the patient was not able to remain still during
the examination or complete the study, due to "severe pain."

COMPARISON:  MRI of ___.

FINDINGS:

The examination is markedly degraded by patient motion artifact.  There is no
gross signal abnormality seen within the cervicomedullary junction or the
cervical spinal cord.  The vertebral alignment is unremarkable.  The neural
foramina could not be assessed as axial images were not acquired, as well as
the severe motion artifact on sagittal images.

At the C2-3 level, there is a small disc bulge without significant spinal
canal stenosis. 

At the C3-4 level, a disc bulge causes remodeling of the ventral surface of
the cord and moderate spinal canal stenosis.  

At the C4-5 level, a disc bulge causes remodeling of the ventral surface of
the cord and mild spinal canal stenosis.  

At the C5-6 level, a disc bulge along with ligamentum flavum thickening causes
moderately severe spinal canal stenosis. 

At the C6-7 level, a disc bulge along with ligamentum flavum thickening causes
moderate spinal canal stenosis.  

At the C7-T1 level, a disc bulge does not produce significant spinal canal
stenosis.

IMPRESSION: Very limited examination, due to lack of axial images as well as
lack of intravenous contrast (apparently due to patient's "severe pain").  

There is multilevel degenerative disease throughout the cervical spine, but no
gross signal abnormality within the cervical spinal cord.

INDICATION:  Orthotopic liver transplant for cryptogenic cirrhosis with
elevated LFTs post-biopsy concerning for biliary process.  Evaluate
vasculature and biliary ductal dilatation.

LIVER ULTRASOUND WITH DOPPLER

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis ___, liver ultrasound ___.

FINDINGS:  This transplanted liver appears normal in echotexture without focal
lesions.  There is no intra- or extra-hepatic biliary ductal dilatation and
the CBD measures 6 mm.  The fluid collection described on the prior CT
examination in the region of the hepatic hilum are not readily evident on this
examination.

There is patency to the hepatic arterial and venous vasculature.  There is now
normal appearance to the arterial waveforms within the main hepatic artery
with peak systolic velocities now within a more normal range.  There is no
ascites.  The spleen is normal in size measuring 10.6 cm.  A right pleural
effusion is present.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No biliary ductal dilatation.
2.  Normal appearance to the main hepatic arterial waveform with decreased
peak systolic velocities compared to the most recent study.  Patent portal and
hepatic veins.
3.  Right pleural effusions.

INDICATION:  ___ man with abdominal pain, liver transplant, status
post ERCP with stent placement ___ with increased abdominal pain, question
stent migration.

COMPARISONS:  Selected images from ERCP ___ and CT abdomen and pelvis
___.

FINDINGS:  Two plastic stents are seen in the biliary tree located in
approximately the same location compared to fluoroscopic spot films from the
endoscopy suite.  A surgical clip is present in the right upper quadrant
consistent with prior cholecystectomy.  Several nondistended loops of small
and large bowel are present.  Surgical clips are seen in the pelvis.  

IMPRESSION:  Two plastic biliary stents located in approximately stable
position.
